title: Who do you look like?
goals: Describe a person's appearance: height, hair, eyes and features such as a beard, freckles or glasses.
Ask and say who someone looks like with What does he look like? and Who does she look like?
Use have and have got to describe appearance and ask How tall...? and What color...?
Identify one person among several with wearing, standing, with and in.
When you can't remember a name or a word, buy time with What do you call it? and Do you mean...?
Talk about fashion: what is in style and what is dated or old-fashioned.

learn.title: look like / look alike / take after
learn.html:
To talk about appearance we use look like. Note: in English, look like works for two different questions.

QuestionAnswerMeaning
What does Hayley look like?She's tall and thin.What is she physically like?
Who does she look like?She looks like her father.Who does she resemble?
Do Hayley and Heather look alike?No, they look totally different.Do they resemble each other?
  • With he / she / it the question uses does and the verb goes back to the base form: What does he look like?
  • look like + person or noun; look alike is used alone, without an object: The twins look alike.
  • take after + family member is used for similarities of character or inherited features: She takes after her mother.

watch.why: After does, the verb goes in the base form.

watch.wrong: How is your sister? (to ask for a physical description)
watch.right: What does your sister look like?
watch.why: How is...? asks about health or condition; to ask about appearance use What ... look like?

watch.wrong: My brother and I look like.
watch.right: My brother and I look alike.
watch.why: Without an object, the correct form is look alike.

watch.wrong: She is looking like her father.
watch.why: Look like is a state verb: simple present, not continuous.

learn.title: have and have got to describe people
learn.html:
To describe appearance you can use have or have got; they mean the same. Have got is very common in speech and is contracted: I've got, she's got.

FormWith haveWith have got
PositiveShe has straight hair.She's got straight hair.
Yes/no questionDoes she have curly hair?(have is preferred with do/does)
Question with WhoWho has curly hair?Who's got curly hair?
Short answerI do.I do. I've got curly hair.
  • She's got means she has got, not she is got.
  • Don't mix them: Does she have...? (not Does she has...?).
  • To describe physical features, use has long hair, with no article.

watch.why: After does, have goes in the base form.
With he / she / it, use has.
Do / does is not used together with have got.
The adjective goes before the noun and without an article.

learn.title: How tall...? and What color...?
learn.html:
To ask about height we use How tall; for the color of hair or eyes, What color. Both use the verb be.

QuestionAnswer
How tall is her father?He's six foot seven. / He's over two meters tall.
What color is Hayley's hair?It's blond.
What color are Hayley's eyes?They're blue.

The verb agrees with what is described: hair is singular (is) and eyes is plural (are). For height, use tall, not high, when talking about people.

watch.why: The question is How tall...?, without much.
For people, use tall, not high.

learn.title: Identifying people: -ing, with, in
learn.html:
To say which person someone is (when you can see them), use short phrases after the man / the woman / the guy / the one.

StructureExample
verb + -ing (what they are doing or wearing)She's the woman standing by the table. / the woman wearing black pants.
by / next to + placeShe's the one by the table.
with + feature or clothingShe's the one with long hair. / The guy with the yellow pants.
in + clothingWho's the guy in the blue shirt?

The -ing form doesn't need who is: the man talking to Rosa (= the man who is talking to Rosa). For clothing, wearing, with and in can all be used.

watch.wrong: She's the girl wear the green dress.
watch.right: She's the girl wearing the green dress.

watch.wrong: He's the boy who talking to Rosa.
watch.right: He's the boy talking to Rosa.
watch.why: Either use who is talking or just talking; never who + -ing.

watch.wrong: The one in glasses is Jason.
watch.right: The one with glasses is Jason.
watch.why: With glasses (a feature) use with; in is for clothing.

watch.wrong: The guy with blue shirt is my brother.
watch.right: The guy in the blue shirt is my brother.
watch.why: For clothing: in the... or wearing the...

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• What does he look like? / Who does he look like? — asking for a description or a resemblance.
  • They look totally different. / They look exactly alike. — comparing two people.
  • Which one is your roommate? — The one with glasses. — identifying someone.
  • Oh, what's his name? / Do you remember that guy? — buying time when you can't remember a name.
  • What do you call it? / What do you call those? — asking for a word you can't remember.
  • Do you mean a goatee? / You mean Max! — suggesting or confirming what is being talked about.
  • Short hair is in. / Long hair is out. — talking about fashion informally.
  • It's fashionable for women to wear... / High heels are dated. — talking about fashion more formally.

write.prompt: Describe two people in your family (120 to 180 words): what they look like (height, hair, eyes, features), who they look like, and how they usually dress. Use look like, have / have got, and at least two sentences with with, in or -ing. Opening: My sister is tall and thin. She looks like...
checklist: 120 to 180 words
At least one sentence with look like or take after
has / 's got with he / she (not "does has")
Adjective before the noun (long curly hair)
Two sentences with with, in or -ing
Appearance vocabulary (bald, freckles, glasses...)
write.model:
My sister is tall and thin. She looks like my mother because they both have long curly black hair and big brown eyes. She has got a lot of freckles on her nose, and she wears glasses. People say she takes after my mom in personality too, because she is kind and patient. She usually dresses in jeans and a white T-shirt, but on weekends she likes wearing colorful skirts.

My uncle Jorge is very different. He is short and a little heavy, and he is bald, so he often wears a baseball cap. He has a gray beard and a friendly smile. I think he looks like my grandfather, but my dad says that he takes after my grandmother because they are both funny. The man with the big laugh in our family photos is always Jorge! He doesn't like formal clothes. He usually wears a shirt with short sleeves and comfortable pants. Last Christmas, I saw him in a red sweater with a reindeer, and everybody was laughing. He has got a great sense of humor.

write.prompt: Write a text of 120 to 180 words about a group photo (a party, a wedding or school): identify four people with phrases like the man wearing..., the one with... Add a short conversation where you can't remember a name (What's his name? / Do you mean...?). End by saying which clothes or hairstyles are in style or out of style today.
checklist: 120 to 180 words
Four people identified (wearing / with / in / by)
A question with What do you call...? or Do you mean...?
Two fashion expressions (in style, out of style, dated, trendy)
Verbs in the correct form (has, looks, is wearing)
write.model:
This is a photo from my cousin's wedding last June. The man wearing the gray suit is my uncle Ramon. Next to him, the woman in the long green dress is my aunt Elena. The girl with the red ribbon in her hair is my little cousin Sofia, and the boy holding the cake is her brother, Diego. At the back, my grandmother is wearing a purple hat.

At the party, I was talking to my friend Pablo when I saw a tall man by the door.
"Who is that man? What's his name?" I asked.
"Do you mean the one with the beard?" Pablo said.
"Yes! I can't remember his name."
"Oh, that's Esteban, the bride's friend."
"Thanks! My memory is terrible."

Looking at the photo today, I laugh at some of the clothes. My uncle's wide tie is out of style now, and the big hair on some of the women looks dated. Nowadays, simple suits and short hairstyles are in style, and people think they are very trendy.

reading.title: The Twins at the Wedding
reading.intro: Read Lena's email about a family wedding and answer.
paragraphs: Hi Carla! Last Saturday I went to my cousin Ana's wedding in Puebla, and I want to tell you about it. It was a big family party, and I met a lot of relatives for the first time.

First, I saw the groom's twin brothers. They are identical twins, so they look exactly alike! Both of them are tall and muscular, and they have short dark hair. At first I couldn't tell them apart. Then my aunt Rosa helped me. She said, "Daniel is the one with a small goatee. Pablo is the one wearing the gray tie." After that, it was easy.

Then I met the bride's grandfather. He is bald, and he has a long white mustache. He is very funny. He says that he takes after his own mother, because she was also short and very talkative. Everybody loves him. Ana, the bride, looks like her mother: they both have curly hair and brown eyes, but Ana is taller. Her mother told me that Ana was a tiny baby with no hair at all!

I also talked to a young woman wearing a long green dress. Her hair was in a ponytail, and she had pierced ears and big silver earrings. She was very friendly. We talked about clothes. She said that short dresses are going out of style, but long dresses are becoming fashionable. I don't agree. I think skinny jeans and sneakers are always trendy, and nobody at the wedding wore baggy pants!

At the end of the party, I tried to remember the name of the photographer. I said, "Who's the man with the long fingernails and the camera? Oh, what's his name?" My uncle laughed and said, "Do you mean Mr. Ortega?" Yes! That was it. He took more than three hundred pictures. I'm sending you the best one. Call me soon, and tell me about your trip! Lena

listening.title: Who's that guy?
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation between two friends at a party. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Hey, Dan! Over here! I can't believe you're here.
Hi, Mia! Wow, I love your new hairstyle. You have a ponytail now!
Thanks! Hey, do you see that guy over there? The one wearing the red shirt?
The tall one with glasses? Yes. Who is he?
I don't remember his name! He was in our class last year. He had a funny little beard. What do you call that?
Do you mean a goatee? Oh, I know. You mean Max!
Yes, Max! But now he doesn't have a goatee. He has short spiked hair.
He looks different. He's not skinny anymore. He's very muscular.
And who is the woman talking to him? She has long curly hair.
That's his sister, Lucy. They look alike, don't they? They have the same dark eyes.
Yes, she looks just like him! Do you want to say hello?
Sure. Let's go. By the way, what color are Max's eyes? I always forget.
They're brown, like his sister's. Come on!
